articles.title: LLM Policies: Progress At All Costs
articles.summary: KDE and GNOME are considering policies for Large Language Models (LLMs) in their projects, with some teams already having strong policies in place. This is not about nitpicking workflows, but rather about the raison d'être of FLOSS projects, with two sides coexisting: collectivism, where FLOSS is about accomplishing things together, and completionism, where FLOSS is about individual technical problems. The collectivist framing rewards social bonding and experiences, while completionism emphasizes individual speed and efficiency. The introduction of LLMs has given the completionist group a lever to stop giving the collectivist framing any room, and progress is now being measured by the LLM's output, rather than human interaction.

articles.title: Pentium II at 600Mhz with Voodoo 3 Emulated on 86Box with M6 Mac Mini
articles.summary: The Pentium II at 600Mhz with Voodoo 3 Emulated on 86Box with M6 Mac Mini is a fascinating project that demonstrates the importance of accurate CPU timing, chipset behavior, and other hardware details to get period software to behave properly. The project's focus on accuracy is expensive, but the practical consequence is that core count barely matters, and what really matters is how fast one core can run and hold that speed without throttling. The M6 Mac Mini's fast cores and ARM-based hardware make it well-suited for this type of project, and the custom 86Box 6.0 build is a testament to the team's efforts.

articles.title: Every package is already installed
articles.summary: Nixpkgs, the package manager for NixOS, has a feature called omnibin that allows every binary shipped with the package to be installed on the system without requiring any additional installation. This is achieved by creating a FUSE filesystem that caches the NARs (Nix Archive) for each package, allowing for lazy loading and on-demand installation. This feature is particularly useful for developers who want to manage their packages without the hassle of installing them individually, and it's also a great example of how Nix can provide a more streamlined and efficient package management system.
